transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ethan Brooks: Ethan here, Vertex Partnerships.
[00:09] Sophie Lee: Sophie, sales director, hey all.
[00:11] Amit Rao: Amit, SE from Vertex.
[00:14] Maya Patel: Great. Carlos and Lina from Redwood?
[00:17] Carlos Ramirez: Carlos, SE.
[00:19] Lina Chen: Lina, CSM.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Sweet. Agenda: quick pipeline review, focus on Acme, then ZenithTech, then technical ask for Acme POC, and close with next steps. Any additions?
[00:30] Sophie Lee: Not from me.
[00:31] Ethan Brooks: All good.
[00:33] Maya Patel: Ok, I'll share my screen in a sec - actually I'll just talk through the spreadsheet we circulated.
[00:38] (brief pause, paper shuffling)
[00:45] Maya Patel: Acme is top priority - currently in "Opportunity" stage, Vertex has the intro, they want Redwood for lower-latency inference and better cost per token than their existing provider. Sophie, can you remind us of the timeline?
[00:58] Sophie Lee: Yeah, Acme wants a pilot by mid-August, decision in September. They have two use-cases - chat support and semantic search for knowledge base. They asked about private deployment (VPC) and SOC2 stuff.
[01:12] Maya Patel: Great, that aligns. Carlos, technical take?
[01:15] Carlos Ramirez: From the notes Amit shared, Acme is concerned about latency at 1-2 second p99 for chat. They also want encryption at rest and key management. Redwood Dedicated should hit that p99 if we tune batching and KV cache; but we'll need to show numbers. I recommend a short benchmark on their payloads - 1000 queries across typical prompt lengths.
[01:36] Amit Rao: They do have long context sometimes, up to 2k tokens. Will that change Dedicated perf?
[01:42] Carlos Ramirez: It'll affect throughput more than p99 latency, but yes kernel selection and quantization profile will matter. We should test both hosted endpoints and Dedicated with our observed sequence length distribution.
[01:53] Maya Patel: Sophie, any procurement constraints?
[01:55] Sophie Lee: Acme requires a vendor questionnaire, SSO, and they want data residency in US. Also they asked about a 45-day PO lead time.
[02:05] Lina Chen: We have SOC2 and can support SAML SSO for enterprise. For data residency, we have US regions available on Hosted and Dedicated.
[02:14] Ethan Brooks: On co-sell economics - Acme is mid-market; they'd expect a partner discount. Vertex usually wants a % split on first-year revenue. What's Redwood's typical co-sell discount?
[02:26] Maya Patel: We generally do tiered discounts depending on pipeline motion. For joint-sourced deals under partner-assist, we can be flexible but need to see ARR numbers. I'll share a proposed discount grid post-call.
[02:36] Sophie Lee: Sounds good. Can we also get an estimate of cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated? That helps us pitch.
[02:44] Carlos Ramirez: I can provide ballpark numbers; but the Dedicated amortized compute plus reserved commit changes cost per token. I'll run cost modelling with the Acme usage profile and share.
[02:55] Maya Patel: Ok, moving to ZenithTech quick note - they're a smaller opportunity, mostly embeddings for semantic search. Vertex thinks it's a low-touch deal.
[03:04] Sophie Lee: Right, we expect a small pilot, likely hosted API is fine, no private deployment ask.
[03:09] Maya Patel: Good. On risks: Acme is evaluating Anthropic and Bedrock as well. We need a clear differentiation: performance per cost and enterprise controls.
[03:19] Ethan Brooks: They mentioned ease of integration too; if Redwood can hand them a working SDK snippet and a starter template it helps.
[03:26] Maya Patel: We have quickstart snippets; I'll add a Vertex-branded starter prompt and example app.
[03:31] Carlos Ramirez: For the POC tech plan: we need sample data, expected qps, target p99, and token distribution. If Vertex can get that from Acme we'll run two comparative runs: Hosted and Dedicated.
[03:44] Amit Rao: I'll coordinate with Acme's engineering to pull logs for sample prompts. Could be messy - logs have PII redaction stuff.
[03:52] Lina Chen: Note on privacy: we can sign an NDA if needed and provide a temp sandbox for logs. Also we can provide guidance for redaction.
[04:00] Sophie Lee: Perfect. On the commercial ask - Acme asked for a joint demo next week with their CTO. Can Redwood support a 30-min demo?
[04:09] Maya Patel: Yes, Carlos can run a short technical demo, and I'll cover the commercial/partnership bits. Which day next week works?
[04:16] Sophie Lee: Wednesday afternoon (PDT) is ideal.
[04:19] Carlos Ramirez: Works for me.
[04:21] Maya Patel: I'll tentatively book Wed 2025-07-30 14:00 PDT, send invite after the call.
[04:26] Ethan Brooks: Great.
[04:28] Maya Patel: Now a quick run through the pipeline spreadsheet - I'll call out stages: Acme (hot), ZenithTech (warm), NovaRetail (cold but long-term). Ethan, any movement on NovaRetail?
[04:39] Ethan Brooks: NovaRetail wants a pilot Q4; no immediate spend. We're keeping them nurtured.
[04:44] Maya Patel: Ok. For Acme, current ask from their side is SLA, SSO, and initial pricing. Sophie, can Vertex push for an intro to procurement?
[04:53] Sophie Lee: Yes, I can do that this week.
[04:56] Maya Patel: On the technical blockers we flagged: long context and encryption. Carlos, is there anything else?
[05:02] Carlos Ramirez: Just that we might need a custom quantization profile if they want to reduce cost without impacting quality. That can take 2-3 weeks to validate but we can do an initial run with default optimized kernels.
[05:15] Amit Rao: Do you have a quick note on how Redwood handles KV cache persistence across sessions? Acme asked about warm start for session contexts.
[05:23] Carlos Ramirez: We have KV cache management; for Dedicated we can expose longer-lived KV cache and there are primitives to persist and rehydrate, but we'd have to scope it in the POC. I'll write a short doc for Amit.
[05:34] Maya Patel: Great. Any competitor intel we should be aware of?
[05:36] Ethan Brooks: They talked about Bedrock pricing being attractive for large-scale inference but less integrated for private deployments. Anthropic is pushing a safety angle.
[05:45] Sophie Lee: Also, one note - Acme's CTO is worried about model drift monitoring; they want quality regressions flagged. Anything we offer there?
[05:54] Lina Chen: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evals/prompt sets. We can show a quick dashboard in the demo.
[06:03] Maya Patel: Ok time check - we've been on 6 minutes - that flew. We'll set concrete owners. I'll summarize: Maya to send updated pipeline + playbook by Monday 7/28; Carlos to schedule benchmark and run two runs; Sophie to intro procurement and Acme contact by 7/29; Lina to schedule follow-up cadence and loop legal for contract template.
[06:21] Ethan Brooks: That captures it.
[06:23] Sophie Lee: One more ask - can Redwood provide a one-pager on co-sell economics we can share with Vertex partner execs?
[06:30] Maya Patel: Yes, I'll include a simple credit split and example discount tier in the doc I send.
[06:35] Carlos Ramirez: I'll also attach a tech checklist for the POC.
[06:38] Maya Patel: Any final Qs?
[06:40] Amit Rao: None from me.
[06:41] Sophie Lee: No.
[06:42] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with invites and docs.
[06:46] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: small transcription artifacts - sometimes "Bedrock" typed as "bedrock" lower case, "Redwood Dedicated" was misspelled in one note as "Redwood Dedictaed" in the shared spreadsheet, and speaker overlap at ~03:31 got merged in the auto transcript.
